p5-79.qa: Check scope and recent changes; CloudWatch dashboards and alarms (ALB 5xx, target health, ECS task restarts, RDS CPU and connections, queue depth); Logs Insights by correlation id; traces; then mitigate (rollback, scale) and fix the root cause.
i: Check AWS Health Dashboard for service issues.
CloudTrail for configuration changes.
ECS stopped task reasons (OOM, health check failures).
Start from the dashboard (errors, latency), correlate with recent deploys, then dig into Logs Insights and traces.
f: Where do you see why an ECS task stopped?
The stopped reason in the ECS console or DescribeTasks.
How do you find who changed a security group?
CloudTrail events.

p5-80.a: Agree RTO and RPO with the business, then pick a strategy: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby or active-active.|Automated backups and cross-region copies, IaC to rebuild, replicated data (RDS cross-region replica, DynamoDB global tables, S3 replication), runbooks and regular DR drills.
p5-80.qa: Agree RTO and RPO with the business, then pick a strategy: backup and restore (cheapest, slowest), pilot light, warm standby or active-active (fastest, most expensive). Automate infrastructure with IaC, replicate data cross-region, and test restores and failovers regularly.
i: AWS Backup for centralised, cross-region, cross-account copies.
RDS cross-region read replicas or snapshots; S3 cross-region replication; DynamoDB global tables.
Runbooks and game days.
Define RPO/RTO first; strategies range from backup/restore to pilot light, warm standby and multi-site active-active.
f: What's the most common DR failure?
Untested backups that don't restore.
Why cross-account backups?
Protection against account compromise or ransomware.

p5-81.a: Automatically adjusting capacity to load: EC2 Auto Scaling groups, ECS service scaling, DynamoDB capacity. Target tracking (keep CPU near 60 percent), step or scheduled scaling; scale out fast, scale in slowly.
p5-81.qa: Autoscaling adjusts capacity to load automatically: EC2 Auto Scaling groups, ECS service scaling, DynamoDB capacity, Lambda concurrency. Target tracking (keep CPU near a target) is simplest; step scaling reacts to alarm thresholds; scheduled scaling handles known peaks; predictive scaling uses forecasts.
i: Scale on the right metric (requests per target, queue depth).
Warm-up and cooldown settings matter.
ECS service autoscaling with target tracking on CPU or ALB requests per target.
Scale-in cooldowns and graceful shutdown avoid dropping in-flight work.
f: Why scale in slowly?
To avoid flapping and keep capacity for returning load.
What is predictive scaling?
Using ML forecasts of traffic to add capacity ahead of time.

p5-82.a: Security group: stateful, attached to instances or ENIs, allow rules only.|NACL: stateless, attached to subnets, allow and deny rules evaluated in order, return traffic must be allowed explicitly.
p5-82.qa: A security group is stateful, attached to instances or ENIs, and has allow rules only; a NACL is stateless, attached to subnets, with allow and deny rules evaluated in number order, so return traffic needs explicit rules. Security groups are the main control; NACLs add a coarse subnet-level guard.
i: Security groups can reference other security groups.
NACLs need ephemeral port ranges for return traffic.
Security groups are stateful and attached to ENIs; NACLs are stateless and apply to subnets.
NACLs need explicit ephemeral-port rules for return traffic.
f: Which to use to block a specific IP?
A NACL deny rule (or WAF).
Stateful meaning?
Return traffic for allowed connections is automatically allowed.

p5-83.a: Lets resources in private subnets make outbound internet calls (package downloads, external APIs) without being reachable inbound; managed and per availability zone, charged per hour and per GB, so use VPC endpoints for AWS services.
p5-83.qa: A NAT Gateway lets resources in private subnets make outbound internet calls (package downloads, external APIs) without being reachable inbound. It's managed and highly available within an AZ, so deploy one per AZ, and watch data processing costs.
i: VPC endpoints avoid NAT costs for AWS services (S3 gateway endpoint is free).
IPv6 uses an egress-only internet gateway instead.
Lets private subnets reach the internet outbound; charged per hour and per GB processed.
VPC endpoints for S3/DynamoDB avoid NAT data charges.
f: Why one per AZ?
An AZ failure would otherwise cut outbound access for other AZs, plus cross-AZ charges.
How do you reduce NAT cost?
VPC endpoints for AWS services and caching dependencies.

p5-84.a: With an ECS task role (or Pod Identity / IRSA on EKS): the SDK credential chain gets temporary credentials automatically; no access keys in images or environment variables; least-privilege policies; VPC endpoints.
p5-84.qa: With an ECS task role (or EKS Pod Identity/IRSA): the SDK credential chain gets temporary credentials automatically, with no access keys in code or images; least-privilege policies scope access, and VPC endpoints keep traffic private.
i: Credentials are served by the container credentials endpoint and rotated automatically.
Separate execution role (ECS agent) from task role (your code).
ECS task roles give each task its own IAM credentials via the container metadata endpoint; the SDK picks them up automatically.
c: var s3 = new AmazonS3Client();   // picks up task role credentials automatically
f: What is IRSA?
IAM Roles for Service Accounts: Kubernetes service accounts mapped to IAM roles via OIDC.
How do you test locally?
Use an SSO profile or assumed role with the same permissions.

p5-85.a: Secrets Manager: built for secrets, automatic rotation (RDS), cross-account sharing, priced per secret.|Parameter Store: config and secrets (SecureString), hierarchical, free standard tier, no built-in rotation.
p5-85.qa: Secrets Manager is built for secrets: automatic rotation (RDS integration), cross-account sharing, versioning, priced per secret per month. Parameter Store holds config and secrets (SecureString with KMS) cheaply with hierarchy, but rotation is manual. I use Secrets Manager for credentials and Parameter Store for configuration.
i: Both integrate with ECS task definitions and .NET configuration providers.
Cache secrets in the app to reduce API calls and cost.
Secrets Manager: rotation, cross-account sharing, per-secret cost; Parameter Store: free standard tier, SecureString with KMS.
We used Secrets Manager for database credentials and Parameter Store for config.
f: Can ECS inject Parameter Store values?
Yes, both can be referenced in the secrets section.
How does rotation affect apps?
Apps must re-read secrets on auth failure or periodically.

p5-86.a: Right-size tasks and instances, autoscaling and scale-to-zero for dev, Savings Plans or Reserved capacity, Spot for non-critical work, S3 lifecycle tiers, delete idle resources, VPC endpoints instead of NAT data, log retention policies, cost tags and budgets.
p5-86.qa: Right-size tasks and instances, use autoscaling and scale-to-zero for dev, Savings Plans or Reserved capacity for steady load, Spot for non-critical work, S3 lifecycle and tiering, log retention, VPC endpoints to cut NAT costs, Graviton (ARM) instances, and Cost Explorer with tags and budgets to find waste.
i: Turn off non-production environments outside working hours.
Delete unattached volumes, old snapshots, idle load balancers.
.NET runs well on ARM64 (Graviton) for up to about 40 percent better price-performance (AWS figure).
Rightsize with Compute Optimizer, Savings Plans for steady load, Graviton, and tagging plus Cost Explorer for accountability.
f: Quick win you'd check first?
CloudWatch log retention and idle non-production resources.
How do you make teams cost-aware?
Tag resources by team and share monthly cost reports.
